answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity costly to forge: require every agent to stake a small bond and build a verifiable history before it can transact. Picture a network graph where each trustworthy agent is a vertex anchored to real work, like basalt bedrock rather than loose sand. Newcomers earn trust gradually through attested contributions, so a single operator spinning up thousands of fake voices finds the cost rising faster than any gain — quantity alone cannot compose a credible sonnet of reputation.
